Unit 1 of 10: The CPU and the Fetch–Decode–Execute Cycle

Key ideas

  • CPU components:
  • ALU (arithmetic logic unit): performs calculations and logical comparisons;
  • CU (control unit): directs operations and decodes instructions;
  • registers: very fast storage inside the CPU.
  • Key registers:
  • PC (program counter): the address of the next instruction;
  • MAR (memory address register): the address being accessed;
  • MDR (memory data register): the data being transferred;
  • IR (instruction register): the current instruction;
  • accumulator (AC): results from the ALU.
  • Buses: the address bus carries addresses; the data bus carries data; the control bus carries signals.
  • The fetch–decode–execute cycle:
  • fetch: PC → MAR; the instruction travels via the MDR into the IR; the PC is incremented;
  • decode: the CU interprets the instruction;
  • execute: the instruction is carried out (for example, by the ALU).
  • Multi-core processors can execute several instruction streams at once.

Worked examples

Example 1: PC = 100. The address 100 is copied into the MAR; the instruction at 100 travels via the data bus into the MDR, then the IR; the PC becomes 101.

Example 2: "ADD 7" is decoded by the CU; the ALU adds the value at address 7 to the accumulator.

Example 3: a quad-core CPU can run four threads in parallel, but a program only speeds up if its tasks can be split.

10-mark exam-style question

(a) State the role of the MAR and the MDR. [2]

(b) Describe the fetch stage of the cycle. [4]

(c) Explain why a dual-core processor may not run a program twice as fast. [4]

Answers:

  • (a) The MAR holds the address of the memory location to be read or written; the MDR holds the data or instruction being transferred to or from memory (A2).
  • (b) The PC's address is copied to the MAR (1). The address is sent along the address bus, and the contents of that location return along the data bus to the MDR (1). The instruction is copied to the IR (1). The PC is incremented to point to the next instruction (1).
  • (c) Some tasks are sequential, so they cannot be split between cores (R2). The cores share memory and the bus, and coordinating them adds overhead (R2).

Common mistakes

  1. Saying the PC holds the current instruction (it holds the address of the next one).
  2. Mixing up the MAR and the MDR.
  3. Forgetting to increment the PC.
  4. Saying the ALU decodes instructions (the CU does).
  5. Assuming more cores always means proportionally faster.

Quick recall

  1. What does the ALU do?
  2. What does the PC hold?
  3. Which bus carries addresses?
  4. Which register holds the current instruction?
  5. Name the three stages of the cycle.

Answers: 1) Arithmetic and logic. 2) The address of the next instruction. 3) The address bus. 4) The IR. 5) Fetch, decode, execute.
